title: Dedicated Serve Guarantee playbook and contract appendix for reserved capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose:
This ticket produces a customer-facing playbook and contract appendix that defines measurable throughput guarantees for Dedicated (reserved) capacity, explains how error budgets are computed and consumed, and documents how autoscaling / fleet controls affect credits and remediation. The output will be used by Sales/Legal for contract language, and by SRE/Support to run escalations and credits calculation.

Problem statement:
Customers buying Dedicated capacity require unambiguous guarantees they can map to product entitlements and remediation. Current drafts in the repo give per-minute RPS figures but lack: (1) a consistent quantile-based measurement approach, (2) a clear error-budget math across rolling windows and burst windows, (3) explicit interplay with autoscaler behavior (ramp, cooldown), and (4) operational steps and dashboards for verifying breaches and calculating credits. This creates negotiation friction and operational ambiguity during incidents.

Proposal (high level):
- SLA metric: "Served-Throughput (tokens/minute or requests/minute, configurable per-customer)" measured as the 95th percentile of minute-level throughput across the SLA observation window (30-day rolling by default).
- Availability/pass threshold: Customer's reserved throughput (committed RPS or tokens/min) is the baseline. A breach occurs when measured Served-Throughput falls below 95% of commitment for a contiguous 10-minute period, or when 95th percentile over 30-day window is < 99% of commitment (tiered detection).
- Error budget: Calculated as the complement of SLA attainment over the rolling window. Example: 30-day window with 99% target leaves a 1% error budget capacity, computed in tokens*minutes. Credits are proportional to the shortfall magnitude and duration.
- Credit formula: Credit = monthly fee * min(0.5, (shortfall_tokens / committed_tokens) * (shortfall_minutes / 43200)) — capped per-contract. Rationale and worked examples included below.
- Autoscale interplay: Reserved capacity autoscaler has an explicit ramp/cooldown contract. If autoscale is configured with a user-controlled ramp > 2 minutes, customer is responsible for configuring burst buffer; otherwise Redwood will honor immediate failover. Credits will be reduced by the fraction of shortfall attributable to user-configured autoscale delay (measured from autoscale events in metrics).
- Fleet controls / isolation modes: Describe three modes: "Dedicated-isolated" (single-tenant pool), "Dedicated-shared" (shared pool for same-customer groups), and "Hybrid-fallback" (fallback to hosted variants). SLA language differs by mode — isolation mode yields stronger guarantees and smaller credit caps.

Worked examples (short):
- Example 1: Customer commits 100k tokens/min sustained. Over a 30-day window, 95th percentile reaches 98k tokens/min -> shortfall 2k = 2%. Error budget consumption = 2% of window -> compute credits as formula.
- Example 2: 15-minute outage where served throughput drops to zero due to AZ network flapping; autoscaler triggered but took 7 minutes to reach target due to configured ramp. We show how to apportion credit between Redwood operational fault and customer-configured ramp.

Operational playbook (for SRE & Support):
1) Detection: Alert when minute-level Served-Throughput < 95% of commitment for > 5 consecutive minutes.
2) Triage: Validate telemetry (Grafana dashboard link), check autoscale events (events API link), and review model variant fallbacks.
3) Attribution: Use event correlation timeline to attribute cause: infra (AZ), autoscaler config (customer or Redwood-managed), model fallback, upstream quota throttles.
4) Credit calculation: Run the calculation notebook (GitHub PR link) to compute provisional credit.
5) Communication: Use contract-ready template (Confluence link) and provide remediation plan.

Contract language snippets (to be reviewed by Legal):
- Definition section: precise definitions for "Committed Throughput", "Served-Throughput", "Observation Window", "Breach Event", "Error Budget" and "Credit Amount".
- Remedies section: explicit credit table mapping percent shortfall x duration to percent-of-monthly-fee credits; maximum aggregate credit per rolling year; exclusions (scheduled maintenance, customer misconfigurations, force majeure).
- Autoscale clause: statement that customer-managed autoscale configuration that knowingly increases ramp/cooldown windows reduces credit eligibility for shortfalls caused within those windows.
- Audit & Verification: Redwood provides measurement artifacts (minute-level time series, autoscale events, and sampling of request traces) within 72 hours of request to support or dispute a claim.

Review feedback/decisions to capture in this ticket:
- We will use tokens/min as primary unit but allow customers to elect requests/min where they have stable per-request token sizes. (Decision: Product)
- Quantiles chosen: 95th for minute-level detection and 99th for monthly rolling. (Decision: SRE & Product — documented here for audit)
- Use of rolling windows instead of calendar months to prevent month-boundary gaming. (Decision: Legal accepted)

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should we offer a "latency-adjusted" credit for customers who care more about p95 latency than throughput? (trade-off: complexity in contract and measurement)
- Cap: recommended cap is 50% of monthly fee per incident year; legal prefers a lower capped number for enterprise deals. Need directive from Revenue Ops.
- Burst allowance: how many minutes of burst > committed throughput should be considered allowable before a breach? (default 5 minutes/week?)

- Calculation notebook (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/dedicated-sla/tree/feature/credits-calc
- Dashboards: Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serve-throughput/dedicated-sla-playbook

Next steps & acceptance criteria:
- Iterate legal-approved wording and circulate to Sales (due 2026-03-19).
- Implement a reference calculation endpoint in ENG-42100 and link automation from billing to produce credits (blocked until ENG-42100 done).
- Add a feature flag for "tokens/min vs requests/min" selection in contract metadata.
- Acceptance: legal sign-off + two e2e simulations that reproduce credit calculations and an internal runbook that SREs can follow within 24 minutes of an incident.

Owner: Marcus Nguyen (PM) — coordinate with Aisha (product), SRE lead, and Legal.

If approved, this appendix will be attached to Dedicated capacity SOWs as "Appendix B: Throughput Commitment & Remediation Playbook."
